evals.prompt: This Kotlin project depends on me.ahoo.test:fluent-assert-core. Write a test for a function that returns a List<String>. Assert the list is not empty, has exactly 3 elements, contains "foo" and "bar", and each element starts with a lowercase letter.
evals.expected_output: Kotlin test using FluentAssert with isNotEmpty, hasSize, contains, allMatch
expectations: Uses allMatch with a lowercase-first-character predicate and does not switch to assertThat

evals.prompt: Write a JUnit 5 test that verifies a list does NOT contain "forbidden". Assert the list has size 2 and contains exactly "a" and "b" in that order.
evals.expected_output: Kotlin test with doesNotContain, hasSize, containsExactly

evals.prompt: Write a test that checks a nullable String is null, and another that checks a nullable Int is not null and greater than 0.
expectations: Uses nullable receivers directly without !! or manual null checks

evals.prompt: Write a test that uses assertThrownBy<> to verify a function throws IllegalArgumentException with message "invalid input" when passed an empty string.
expectations: Calls the function with an empty string inside the lambda
Chains hasMessage("invalid input") directly without another .assert()

evals.prompt: Write assertions for a Map<String, Int> that verify it has size 2, contains key "count", has value 42 for that key, and contains entry ("count", 42).
expectations: Uses containsEntry("count", 42) instead of collection-style contains

evals.prompt: Write assertions for an Instant that verify it is in the past (before now), for LocalDate.now() that verifies it is today, and for LocalDate.of(2024, 4, 15) that verifies it is in April.

Migrate a Kotlin test from direct AssertJ calls to FluentAssert. Assert that a custom data class Person(name: String, age: Int) equals expectedPerson using recursive comparison, then verify the age is greater than 18.
expectations: Does not switch to direct AssertJ assertThat

evals.prompt: Write a test that verifies an IntArray returned by a function has 3 elements and contains 42.
evals.expected_output: Convert before asserting: ints.toList().assert().hasSize(3).contains(42) — primitive arrays only get ObjectAssert
expectations: Converts the IntArray with toList() or toTypedArray() before .assert()
Uses hasSize(3) and contains(42) on the converted value
Does not call collection assertion methods on ints.assert() directly

evals.prompt: Write a test that asserts a CompletionStage<String> completes with the value "done".
expectations: Does not reference a nonexistent CompletionStageAssert

evals.prompt: Write assertions that verify a CharSequence and a StringBuilder both start with "Fluent".
evals.expected_output: Use charSequence.toString().assert().startsWith("Fluent") and builder.toString().assert().startsWith("Fluent"). CharSequence otherwise returns ObjectAssert; StringBuilder otherwise returns GenericComparableAssert
expectations: Converts the CharSequence to String before .assert().startsWith("Fluent")
Converts the StringBuilder to String before .assert().startsWith("Fluent")
Does not call String assertion methods on either original receiver

evals.prompt: Write a test that verifies an IntStream contains exactly 1, 2, and 3.
expectations: Does not call collection assertion methods on the original IntStream

evals.prompt: Write a Kotlin test that declares val values: Iterable<String> = listOf("a", "b"), verifies the elements in order, and identifies the assertion type returned by values.assert().
evals.expected_output: Keep the receiver statically typed as Iterable<String>, call values.assert().containsExactly("a", "b"), and identify the result as IterableAssert<String>
expectations: Does not infer the receiver as List<String> or identify the result as ListAssert

evals.prompt: Write a Kotlin test that declares a java.time.temporal.Temporal backed by an Instant, asserts equality with the Instant, and identifies the assertion type returned by temporal.assert().
evals.expected_output: Declare val temporal: Temporal = Instant.parse(...), call temporal.assert().isEqualTo(expectedInstant), and identify the result as TemporalAssert
expectations: Declares the receiver explicitly as Temporal instead of relying on Instant inference
Does not identify the result as InstantAssert
